## Summary of Experimental Insights

Successful experiments, like the Dragonnet on IHDP, share a pattern of clear problem framing, robust baseline comparison, and careful implementation without code bugs, yielding a 69% MAE reduction. Key success factors include selecting appropriate datasets with known ground truth, using validated architectures, and ensuring metric transparency. Common failure patterns include overfitting to small datasets, ignoring covariate shift, and insufficient hyperparameter tuning—often masked by code bugs or poor evaluation splits. Another pitfall is conflating prediction accuracy with causal inference validity. For future experiments, prioritize rigorous data preprocessing, especially for high-dimensional confounders, and always report uncertainty intervals. Use simpler baselines before complex models to establish realistic improvement thresholds. Implement cross-validation and sensitivity analyses to detect hidden biases. Automate unit tests for data pipelines and loss functions. Finally, document all hyperparameter choices and failed configurations to avoid redundant dead ends.
